gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 diagnoses instability and boundary misidentification in the inner finite-grid set limit. It does not recognize the distinct failure that the proved regularized strict-sublevel target is not the stated closed target C_ap,ε, nor the missing equality or outer-limit repair.

Both identify the unsupported fixed-n2 set-limit claim caused by strict threshold membership under mere pointwise numerical convergence, including possible oscillation at equality and the need for threshold stabilization/slack.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The strict finite-grid threshold decisions need not stabilize under pointwise convergence when a limiting value lies on the cutoff, so the asserted set limit and subsequent tower construction are unjustified without an explicit stabilization or slack construction.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of the asserted finite-set limit and its strict-threshold identification under pointwise convergence, with a required stabilization/slack repair.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly gives the oscillating-boundary countermechanism, states that the set limit may fail to exist or be misidentified, and supplies a finite-grid threshold-slack repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that without full support the L1 quantity is only a seminorm on the finite-dimensional subspace, so its unit set need not be sup-norm compact and the claimed uniform quadrature/F2 conclusion fails; both provide the corresponding full-support or injectivity repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof incorrectly treats the L1 seminorm as a genuine norm on arbitrary finite-dimensional subspaces of C(X) under an arbitrary finite measure; null directions can make the normalized set sup-norm unbounded and invalidate uniform quadrature convergence.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of F2/uniform quadrature for arbitrary finite-dimensional dictionaries when the measure lacks full support because L1 has nonzero null directions and the normalized set is not sup-norm compact.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 states the missing full-support hypothesis, gives the same null-direction example and unbounded normalized set, identifies the false uniform convergence, and supplies the full-support repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns arbitrary countable oracle evaluations being non-Borel and therefore invalidating a base-case Borelness argument. It does not identify the diagonal impossibility of a universal Borel evaluator for all Borel characteristic functions on an uncountable standard Borel space, nor repair the analytic projection construction.

Both identify that the greedy star-priority construction can be killed by unrelated dead-end branches despite Silver-tree containment, so the forward Silver-to-spectrum implication and equivalence fail.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The greedy witness recursion does not preserve a Silver witness in the presence of unrelated dead ends; it can reach bottom and produce bounded periods, so a non-torsion approximate eigenvalue is not obtained even when the input tree contains the required Silver tree.

component_coverage.gold_component: False greedy maximality/forward Silver-tree spectral implication, demonstrated by a tree containing a Silver tree but whose greedy recursion reaches bottom and loses the non-torsion spectrum.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 supplies the same dead-end counterexample, computes the greedy patterns reaching bottom, derives failure of the approximate-spectrum conclusion, and explains that a new construction is required.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 notes that the recursion reaches bottom and that the spectral equivalence fails, but it does not diagnose the separate definitional failure that the odometer is undefined on the bottom symbol, nor provide an explicit bottom-branch definition for the map.

ISSUE-005 concerns failure of the greedy Silver-tree reduction. It does not recognize the distinct countable-block spectral error that approximate spectrum can arise from vectors in varying blocks without belonging to the closure of the union of block spectra, or the required uniform resolvent condition.
